notes: Every filled value names its source id in the crop's 'sources' map; fields still needing research are listed in 'todo' and set to null.
Season windows are USDA 'most active' planting/harvest spans (MM-DD). Crop 'year' in a rotation = its harvest year, so winter wheat is planted the fall before.
Kc ini values are FAO-56 Table 12 crop-group values (the per-crop column is an image on the FAO page).
Where a source gives a range, it is kept as [low, high]; scoring (Step 8) decides which end applies.
ky (FAO-33 seasonal yield response factor) replaces the plan's 1-5 drought_tolerance: ky > 1 = yield drops more than the water deficit (drought sensitive), ky < 1 = tolerant.

base_temp_c and heat_threshold_c are MEAN daily temperatures (USDA TB1935 Table 5.1, diurnal range up to 10 C); heat_threshold_c is the reproductive-stage failure (ceiling) temperature, not a daily maximum.

gdd_required uses the same 86/50 F method as climate_shift.py, in C-days (F-days x 5/9). Only corn has a sourced value; soybean flowering is daylength-driven (FAO) and wheat needs vernalization, so a base-10 C GDD total does not apply to them.

n_effect follows K-State MF2586 (Jan 2024), in its units: need_lb_n_per_unit = lb fertilizer N per unit of expected yield (ie/fe with non-irrigated ie and default fe 0.55 where the formula has them); next_crop_adjust_lb_n_ac = this crop's 'previous crop adjustment' to the next crop's N rate (negative = credit), split by whether the next crop is warm- or cool-season. Alfalfa uses the 'good stand' row.
soil_preferences textures use the USDA class names from soil_client.texture_class.

crops.name: Corn (grain)
crops.soil_note: FAO: does well on most soils but less so on very heavy dense clay and very sandy soils; susceptible to waterlogging.

crops.name: Soybean
crops.gdd_note: Not applicable: FAO describes soybean as a short-day plant whose flowering depends on daylength.
crops.soil_note: FAO: wide range of soils except very sandy; sensitive to waterlogging; optimum pH 6 to 6.5.

crops.name: Winter wheat
crops.kc_note: FAO row 'Winter wheat, with frozen soils'
crops.gdd_note: Not applicable: winter wheat needs vernalization over winter, so a base-10 C season total does not describe it.
crops.soil_note: FAO: wide range of soils but medium textures are preferred; optimum pH 6 to 8.

crops.name: Sorghum (grain)
crops.soil_note: FAO: does well on most soils but better in light to medium textured soils; preferably well-aerated and well-drained.

crops.name: Alfalfa (hay)
crops.season_note: USDA lists cutting dates only; harvest window = cutting season. Treated as spring-seeded.
crops.kc_note: FAO row 'Alfalfa hay, averaged cutting effects'
crops.heat_note: Hay crop: no grain-set stage, so the reproductive failure temperature does not apply.
crops.soil_note: UMN: prefers well-drained, deep soils; keeping pH between 6.5 and 7.0 is extremely important.

crops.name: Sunflower
crops.soil_note: FAO: grown on a wide range of soils; under low rainfall needs a deep soil with good water holding capacity; optimum pH 6.0 to 7.5.

crops.name: Cereal rye
crops.cover_note: min_days_before_first_frost = 0 is our reading of SARE's 'late fall is tolerated'; rye survives to spring even when planted late.

crops.name: Crimson clover

cover.timing: mid-fall, at least two weeks before average frost

crops.cover_note: SARE: overwinters in the southern Corn Belt but not the northern Corn Belt; treated as winter-killed in Iowa.
